artifacts.summary: Verifies the 187-line dead-command-recommendation figure, determines the new lint's scope/convention per adoption-lint-conventions.md (full-corpus scope, zero-tolerance landing), confirms lint-routing-wiring.sh/lint-contract-compliance.sh are non-natural hosts, verifies the 46-command valid-set enumeration mechanics (exclude README.md), confirms command-output.md's structural fix has no downstream consumer, and specifies the required gate-24 wiring and fixture-test conventions.

memory_candidates.content: agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/adoption-lint-conventions.md governs lint design in this repo with two rules: (1) non-zero migration debt at landing selects the allowlist convention, debt retired to zero within the same task/landing selects zero-tolerance (no allowlist); (2) adoption lints (hand-rolled-code-pattern class) scope to executable surfaces only (scripts/*.sh, plus *.md restricted to commands/skills/agents) -- docs/ and context/ are out of scope BY CONSTRUCTION for that class. A content-correctness lint (where prose itself, not just code, is the defect -- e.g. a doc rendering a dead command recommendation) is a DIFFERENT class and must use full-corpus scope instead; requirement (2) does not transfer to it even though the doc's framing reads as totalizing ('every adoption lint in this repo must satisfy').

In this repo, every scripts/lint/*.sh gate must be wired into verify-deploy.sh (a new gateN_run() function) AND gate-registry.data (one new tab-separated row) to actually run in CI/deploy verification -- a lint script alone, with no gate wiring, is never exercised by the gate battery. By contrast, a new scripts/tests/test-*.sh fixture file needs NO registration: tests/run-all.sh auto-discovers every scripts/tests/test-*.sh per extension via a glob at runtime.
